_comment: Prior encounter notes per patient, oldest first: what earlier clinicians wrote, stored by the EHR. They are memory about the patient, not state: fallible, expiring, with a hand-written summary as the precomputed variant (R-18). A note that records a vital asserts vitals.bp, so the application can declare a conflict with today's telemetry.

notes.author: dr_lee
notes.summary: March 2026 review: diabetes stable on metformin, foot and eye checks done, no complications.
notes.text: Routine diabetes review with Rosa Delgado. HbA1c 7.1% in February. Continues metformin 500 mg twice daily with good tolerance; no hypoglycaemia reported. Annual foot examination normal, monofilament intact bilaterally; retinal screening March 2026 reported no retinopathy. Discussed carbohydrate distribution across meals and encouraged regular walking. Plan: continue current therapy, repeat HbA1c in six months, annual labs in September.

notes.author: rn_okafor
notes.summary: Intake 28 September: BP 150/95 at nurse intake, patient anxious after a rushed arrival; recheck requested at next visit.
notes.text: Nurse intake for Rosa Delgado ahead of the October follow-up. Blood pressure 150/95 measured once, seated, after the patient arrived hurried and reported feeling anxious about parking. Heart rate 88. Patient declined a repeat reading because she was late for work. Advised that the reading be repeated at the next visit before any change to treatment. Medication list reconciled: metformin 500 mg twice daily, no new medicines, no over-the-counter products.

notes.author: dr_lee
notes.summary: September labs: HbA1c 7.4%, eGFR 78; metformin dose unchanged pending follow-up.
notes.text: Phone call to Rosa Delgado with September results. HbA1c has risen from 7.1% to 7.4%; eGFR 78 mL/min, stable; lipids within target. Discussed that the rise is modest and that the follow-up visit in October will review diet, activity and whether the metformin dose should increase. No change made today. Patient reports no side effects.

notes.author: dr_lee
notes.summary: November 2025: travel vaccinations given, no chronic conditions, no regular medicines.
notes.text: Daniel Mbeki attended for travel vaccinations before a trip to Kenya. No chronic conditions, no regular medicines, no known drug allergies. Hepatitis A and typhoid vaccines administered without reaction. Malaria prophylaxis discussed and prescribed as a one-off course.

notes.author: dr_lee
notes.summary: June 2025: discussed statin; patient declined for now.
notes.text: Discussed lipid results with Rosa Delgado and the option of a statin given diabetes. Patient wished to try dietary change first and declined for now; to revisit in a year.
